{{Short description|2026 cybersecurity incident affecting Canvas LMS}}
The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident and outage affecting Canvas LMS, a learning management system operated by [[Instructure]]. In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref>{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

On May 7, 2026, Canvas was placed under maintenance during a wider outage affecting schools and universities. The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and threatened to release data unless payment demands were met.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref>{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref>{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain iidentifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved..<ref>{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Ttest were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach had not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Impact and responsee ==
Educational institutions in the United States and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The University of California said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access “out of an abundance of caution.”<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that Sacramento State students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref>{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the University of Pennsylvania, Wake County Public Schools, and Duke University.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref>{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

{{Short description|2026 cybersecurity incident affecting Canvas LMS}}{{Current|date=May 2026|2=current cybersecurity incident}}[[File:ShinyHunters Hacking Message.png|thumb|Image of message that appeared on the Canvas webpage for students logging in on May 7, 2026.]]
The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting Canvas LMS, a learning management system operated by [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref>{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, having their web page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]]—a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless ransom payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref>{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref>{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref>{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Ttest were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach had not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The University of California said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that Sacramento State students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref>{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the University of Pennsylvania, Wake County Public Schools, and Duke University.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref>{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

{{Short description|2026 cybersecurity incident affecting Canvas LMS}}{{Current|date=May 2026|2=current cybersecurity incident}}[[File:ShinyHunters Hacking Message.png|thumb|Image of message that appeared on the Canvas webpage for students logging in on May 7, 2026.]]
The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting Canvas LMS, a learning management system operated by [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, having their web page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]]—a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless ransom payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach had not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The University of California said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that Sacramento State students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the University of Pennsylvania, Wake County Public Schools, and Duke University.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, having its web page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]]—a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure (Canvas parent company) and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless [[ransom]] payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach had not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, with its login page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]], a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless [[ransom]] payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, with its login page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]], a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless [[ransom]] payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, with its login page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]], a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless [[ransom]] payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

{{Short description|2026 cybersecurity incident affecting Canvas LMS}}{{Current|date=May 2026|2=current cybersecurity incident}}[[File:ShinyHunters Hacking Message.png|thumb|Image of message that appeared on the Canvas webpage for students logging in on May 7, 2026.]]
The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, with its login page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]], a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless [[ransom]] payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, with its login page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]], a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless [[ransom]] payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC (the Australian Broadcasting Corporation) News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed no evolvement, however there are unconfirmed reports that students have been asking the prime minister to quote "delay my finals, theres a hamas tunnel inside Instructures server banks"... more to come.

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, with its login page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]], a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless [[ransom]] payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States, New Zealand and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC (the Australian Broadcasting Corporation) News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, with its login page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]], a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless [[ransom]] payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States, New Zealand and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC (the Australian Broadcasting Corporation) News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>
