The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, with its login page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]], a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless [[ransom]] payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States, New Zealand and Australia reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC (the Australian Broadcasting Corporation) News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, 2026, Canvas was hacked, with its login page replaced with a message by [[ShinyHunters]], a criminal hacking group. ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for breaching Instructure and Canvas, threatening to release sensitive data unless [[ransom]] payment demands are fulfilled by May 12, 2026.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[File:Canvas logo2.png|thumb|Canvas LMS's logo]]
Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities in the United States for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/> ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> It has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8000 institutions as customers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company stated that it had not found evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final-exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 7, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States, New Zealand, Australia and the Netherlands reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref>

CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, ABC (the Australian Broadcasting Corporation) News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/>

In the Netherlands, 44 educational insitutions have been affected. According to the umbrella organisation [[Universities of the Netherlands]], no university has been approached for ransom. <ref name="NL">{{cite web |title=Thousands of Dutch Students and Teachers Affected by ShinyHunters Hack |website=Dutch Times |date=2026-05-07 |url=https://dutchtimes.nl/news/netherlands/thousands-of-dutch-students-and-teachers-affected-by-shinyhunters-hack/ |access-date=2026-05-08}}</ref>

ShinyHunters threatened to relase Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}} As of May 8, however, Instructure itself reported on their status page no incidents whatsoever related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.{{Cite web|title=Instructure Status|date=2026-05-08|access-date=2026-05-08|url=https://status.instructure.com/|website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}} == Background == Canvas has more than 30 million global active users, with more than 8,000 institutions as customers.{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }} Canvas is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities in the United States for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students. ''Inside Higher Ed'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}} == Breach and outage == Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages amongst users. {{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}. The company stated that it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved. On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into "scheduled" maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}} The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 8, 2026. == Impact and response == Educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, New Zealand, Australia, Sweden, and the Netherlands reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}} CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid. ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}} In Australia, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC]] News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response. In the Netherlands, 44 educational insitutions have been affected. According to the umbrella organisation [[Universities of the Netherlands]], no university has been approached for ransom.{{cite web |title=Thousands of Dutch Students and Teachers Affected by ShinyHunters Hack |website=Dutch Times |date=2026-05-07 |url=https://dutchtimes.nl/news/netherlands/thousands-of-dutch-students-and-teachers-affected-by-shinyhunters-hack/ |access-date=2026-05-08}} In response, several universities disconnected Canvas from their internal systems.{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title=Universiteiten koppelen systemen los na hack, gevolgen voor onderwijs |url=https://www.telegraaf.nl/binnenland/universiteiten-koppelen-systemen-los-na-hack-gevolgen-voor-onderwijs/151233814.html |access-date=8 May 2026 |publisher=Telegraaf |date=2026-05-08 |language=Dutch |trans-title=Universities disconnect systems after hack, consequences for education}} == See also == * [[Cyberattack]] * [[Data breach]] * [[Instructure]] == References == {{reflist}} == External links == * [https://status.instructure.com/ Status on Instructure's website] {{Hacking in the 2020s}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Canvas security incident, 2026}} [[Category:2026 data breaches]] [[Category:2026 in computing]] [[Category:May 2026]] [[Category:Cyberattacks]]

The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}} CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid. ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}} In Australia, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC]] News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response. Any and all attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}} SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}} In Australia, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC]] News reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure itself reported on their status page no incidents whatsoever related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Instructure Status|date=2026-05-08|access-date=2026-05-08|url=https://status.instructure.com/|website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

The hack is the largest educational security breach on record, given that Canvas is used by 41% of higher academia in the US alone and some [[K-12]] schools<ref name=m404>{{cite web|url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/|title=The biggest student data privacy disaster in history: Canvas hack shows the danger of centralized edtech}}</ref> with  8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions being attacked worldwide. ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (some 275 million records), including private messages between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://thetechmarketer.com/canvas-hacked-instructure-shinyhunters-2026/|title=Canvas Hacked Instructure ShinyHunters 2026: 5 Alarming Facts for Students|date=May 8, 2026}}</ref>

The affair came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page. Despite the sensitivity of some of their messages, and the sheer scope of the data compromised, and the [[single point of failure]], they had not been previously informed of any issues whatsoever with the platform.<ref>https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/</ref>

The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure itself reported on their status page no incidents whatsoever related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Instructure Status|date=2026-05-08|access-date=2026-05-08|url=https://status.instructure.com/|website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

Despite the sensitivity of some of their messages, and the sheer scope of the data compromised, and the [[single point of failure]], they had not been previously informed of any issues whatsoever with the platform.<ref>https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/</ref>

Educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, New Zealand,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/education/594635/new-zealand-students-details-caught-up-in-massive-global-university-hack|title=New Zealand students' details caught up in massive global university hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=RNZ}}</ref> Australia,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234|title=Major data breach sees student details compromised|date=May 7, 2026|via=www.abc.net.au}}</ref> Sweden,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.slu.se/en/news/2026/canvasincident/|title=Information about a cybersecurity incident related to Canvas | slu.se|website=www.slu.se}}</ref> and the Netherlands<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613564-universiteiten-en-hogescholen-blokkeren-studie-app-canvas-na-hack|title=Universiteiten en hogescholen blokkeren studie-app Canvas na hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=nos.nl}}</ref> reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC News]] reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/> Several universities including [[University of Technology Sydney]], [[Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology]], and [[Griffith University]], are offering extensions on assignments to affected students. University of Technology Sydney and the [[Department of Education (Queensland)|Queensland Department of Education]] have temporarily disabled access to Canvas systems as a preventative measure until the situation is resolved and are warning staff and students of potential [[phishing]] or scam emails.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=Students receive ransom messages after learning system cyberattack |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-08/students-lose-access-to-canvas-receive-ransom-messages/106657440 |access-date=2026-05-08 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref>

In the Netherlands, 44 educational institutions have been affected.<ref name="NL">{{cite web |title=Thousands of Dutch Students and Teachers Affected by ShinyHunters Hack |website=Dutch Times |date=2026-05-07 |url=https://dutchtimes.nl/news/netherlands/thousands-of-dutch-students-and-teachers-affected-by-shinyhunters-hack/ |access-date=2026-05-08}}</ref>  Several universities disconnected Canvas from their internal systems.<ref name="Telegraaf">{{cite news |last1=<!--- No author named ---> |first1=<!--- No author named ---> |title=Universiteiten koppelen systemen los na hack, gevolgen voor onderwijs |url=https://www.telegraaf.nl/binnenland/universiteiten-koppelen-systemen-los-na-hack-gevolgen-voor-onderwijs/151233814.html |access-date=8 May 2026 |publisher=Telegraaf |date=2026-05-08 |language=Dutch |trans-title=Universities disconnect systems after hack, consequences for education}}</ref>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure itself reported on their status page no incidents whatsoever related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Instructure Status|date=2026-05-08|access-date=2026-05-08|url=https://status.instructure.com/|website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

The hack is the largest educational security breach on record, given that Canvas is used by 41% of higher academia in the US alone and some [[K-12]] schools<ref name=m404>{{cite web|url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/|title=The biggest student data privacy disaster in history: Canvas hack shows the danger of centralized edtech}}</ref> with  8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions being attacked worldwide. ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (some 275 million records), including private messages between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://thetechmarketer.com/canvas-hacked-instructure-shinyhunters-2026/|title=Canvas Hacked Instructure ShinyHunters 2026: 5 Alarming Facts for Students|date=May 8, 2026}}</ref>

The affair came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page. Despite the sensitivity of some of their messages, and the sheer scope of the data compromised, and the [[single point of failure]], they had not been previously informed of any issues whatsoever with the platform.<ref>https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/</ref>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure itself reported on their status page no incidents whatsoever related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Instructure Status|date=2026-05-08|access-date=2026-05-08|url=https://status.instructure.com/|website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

The hack is the largest educational security breach on record as of May 8, 2026, given that Canvas is used by 41% of higher academia in the US alone and some [[K-12]] schools<ref name=m404>{{cite web|url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/|title=The biggest student data privacy disaster in history: Canvas hack shows the danger of centralized edtech}}</ref> with 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions being attacked worldwide. ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (some 275 million records), including private messages between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://thetechmarketer.com/canvas-hacked-instructure-shinyhunters-2026/|title=Canvas Hacked Instructure ShinyHunters 2026: 5 Alarming Facts for Students|date=May 8, 2026}}</ref>

The affair came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page. Despite the sensitivity of some of their messages, the sheer scope of the data compromised, and the [[single point of failure]], they had not been previously informed of any issues whatsoever with the platform.<ref>https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/</ref>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure itself reported on their status page no incidents whatsoever related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Instructure Status|date=2026-05-08|access-date=2026-05-08|url=https://status.instructure.com/|website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

The hack is the largest educational security breach on record as of May 8, 2026, given that Canvas is used by 41% of higher academia in the US alone and some [[K-12]] schools<ref name=m404>{{cite web|url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/|title=The biggest student data privacy disaster in history: Canvas hack shows the danger of centralized edtech}}</ref> with 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions being attacked worldwide. ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (some 275 million records), including private messages between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://thetechmarketer.com/canvas-hacked-instructure-shinyhunters-2026/|title=Canvas Hacked Instructure ShinyHunters 2026: 5 Alarming Facts for Students|date=May 8, 2026}}</ref>

The affair came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page. Despite the sensitivity of some of their messages, the sheer scope of the data compromised, and the [[single point of failure]], they had not been previously informed of any issues whatsoever with the platform.<ref>https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/</ref>

== Background ==
Canvas has more than 30 million global active users, and is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities in the United States for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref> ''[[Inside Higher Ed]]'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages between users.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The company stated that it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into "scheduled" maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

Contact information via the [[end-to-end encryption]] protocol [[Tox (protocol)|T0X]] to a [[.onion]] address is then given.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://github.com/pete-builds/research-reports/blob/main/canvas-instructure-breach-may-2026.md|title=research-reports/canvas-instructure-breach-may-2026.md at main · pete-builds/research-reports|website=GitHub}}</ref>

ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 8, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Impact and response ==
Educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, New Zealand,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/education/594635/new-zealand-students-details-caught-up-in-massive-global-university-hack|title=New Zealand students' details caught up in massive global university hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=RNZ}}</ref> Australia,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234|title=Major data breach sees student details compromised|date=May 7, 2026|via=www.abc.net.au}}</ref> Sweden,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.slu.se/en/news/2026/canvasincident/|title=Information about a cybersecurity incident related to Canvas | slu.se|website=www.slu.se}}</ref> and the Netherlands<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613564-universiteiten-en-hogescholen-blokkeren-studie-app-canvas-na-hack|title=Universiteiten en hogescholen blokkeren studie-app Canvas na hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=nos.nl}}</ref> reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref> Affected academic institutions alone include, but are not limited to, [[Harvard University]], [[Brown University]], [[Pennsylvania State University]], [[University of Illinois]], [[James Madison University]], [[Columbia University]], [[Georgetown University]], [[Oregon State University]], [[University of Michigan]], [[Rutgers University]], [[University of California]], [[University of Chicago]], [[Baylor University]], [[University of Maryland]], [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[University of Oklahoma]], [[University of Iowa]], [[Iowa State University]], [[Texas Tech University]], [[Northwest Arkansas Community College]], [[Virginia Tech]] and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ladbible.com/news/us-news/canvas-hack-shinyhunters-ransom-cyberattack-schools-047514-20260508|title=Hackers ShinyHunters send ransom notes to 9,000 schools as part of cyberattack impacting millions|date=May 8, 2026|website=LADbible}}</ref> 
 
ABC15 reported that finals were disrupted at [[Arizona State University]], with end-of-school activities and celebrations temporarily halted and ASU themselves saying, "ASU is aware of an incident that has affected Canvas, the online platform students and faculty use to access courses and submit work, that has resulted today in users being redirected and rendering the platform inaccessible at this time. This incident is unrelated to any ASU-managed system."<ref>{{cite news |last1=AP via Scripps News Group |title=Cyberattack on Canvas disrupts finals for ASU students and thousands of others worldwide |url=https://www.abc15.com/science-and-tech/cyberattack-on-canvas-disrupts-finals-for-thousands-of-students-worldwide |access-date=8 May 2026 |agency=ABC 15 Arizona |date=8 May 2026}}</ref>
CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained, and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC News]] reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/> Several universities, including [[University of Technology Sydney]], [[Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology]], and [[Griffith University]], are offering extensions on assignments to affected students. University of Technology Sydney and the [[Department of Education (Queensland)|Queensland Department of Education]] have temporarily disabled access to Canvas systems as a preventative measure until the situation is resolved and are warning staff and students of potential [[phishing]] or scam emails.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=Students receive ransom messages after learning system cyberattack |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-08/students-lose-access-to-canvas-receive-ransom-messages/106657440 |access-date=2026-05-08 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref>

In the Netherlands, 44 educational institutions have been affected.<ref name="NL">{{cite web |title=Thousands of Dutch Students and Teachers Affected by ShinyHunters Hack |website=Dutch Times |date=2026-05-07 |url=https://dutchtimes.nl/news/netherlands/thousands-of-dutch-students-and-teachers-affected-by-shinyhunters-hack/ |access-date=2026-05-08}}</ref>  Several universities disconnected Canvas from their internal systems.<ref name="Telegraaf">{{cite news |last1=<!--- No author named ---> |first1=<!--- No author named ---> |title=Universiteiten koppelen systemen los na hack, gevolgen voor onderwijs |url=https://www.telegraaf.nl/binnenland/universiteiten-koppelen-systemen-los-na-hack-gevolgen-voor-onderwijs/151233814.html |access-date=8 May 2026 |publisher=Telegraaf |date=2026-05-08 |language=Dutch |trans-title=Universities disconnect systems after hack, consequences for education}}</ref>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure itself reported on their status page no incidents whatsoever related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Instructure Status|date=2026-05-08|access-date=2026-05-08|url=https://status.instructure.com/|website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

The hack is the largest educational security breach on record as of May 8, 2026, given that Canvas is used by 41% of higher academia in the US alone and some [[K-12]] schools<ref name=m404>{{cite web|url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/|title=The biggest student data privacy disaster in history: Canvas hack shows the danger of centralized edtech}}</ref> with 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions being attacked worldwide. ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (some 275 million records), including private messages between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://thetechmarketer.com/canvas-hacked-instructure-shinyhunters-2026/|title=Canvas Hacked Instructure ShinyHunters 2026: 5 Alarming Facts for Students|date=May 8, 2026}}</ref>

The affair came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure itself reported on their status page no incidents whatsoever related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Instructure Status|date=2026-05-08|access-date=2026-05-08|url=https://status.instructure.com/|website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

The affair came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure itself reported on their status page no incidents whatsoever related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Instructure Status|date=2026-05-08|access-date=2026-05-08|url=https://status.instructure.com/|website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

The affair came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page. The [[University of California]] said Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution."<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref> Affected academic institutions in the US alone include, but are not limited to, [[Brown University]], [[Harvard University]], [[Pennsylvania State University]], [[University of Illinois]], [[James Madison University]], [[Columbia University]], [[Georgetown University]], [[Oregon State University]], [[University of Michigan]], [[Rutgers University]], [[University of California]], [[University of Chicago]], [[Baylor University]], [[University of Maryland]], [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[University of Oklahoma]], [[University of Iowa]], [[Iowa State University]], [[Texas Tech University]], [[Northwest Arkansas Community College]], [[Virginia Tech]] and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ladbible.com/news/us-news/canvas-hack-shinyhunters-ransom-cyberattack-schools-047514-20260508|title=Hackers ShinyHunters send ransom notes to 9,000 schools as part of cyberattack impacting millions|date=May 8, 2026|website=LADbible}}</ref> 
 
ABC15 reported that finals were disrupted at [[Arizona State University]], with end-of-school activities and celebrations temporarily halted and ASU themselves saying, "ASU is aware of an incident that has affected Canvas, the online platform students and faculty use to access courses and submit work, that has resulted today in users being redirected and rendering the platform inaccessible at this time. This incident is unrelated to any ASU-managed system."<ref>{{cite news |title=Cyberattack on Canvas disrupts finals for ASU students and thousands of others worldwide |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tr5aDB2BDxM |access-date=8 May 2026 |agency=ABC15 Arizona |date=8 May 2026}}</ref>
CBS Sacramento reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained, and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="auto2"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC News]] reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="auto1"/> Several universities, including [[University of Technology Sydney]], [[Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology]], and [[Griffith University]], are offering extensions on assignments to affected students. University of Technology Sydney and the [[Department of Education (Queensland)|Queensland Department of Education]] have temporarily disabled access to Canvas systems as a preventative measure until the situation is resolved and are warning staff and students of potential [[phishing]] or scam emails.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=Students receive ransom messages after learning system cyberattack |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-08/students-lose-access-to-canvas-receive-ransom-messages/106657440 |access-date=2026-05-08 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref>

In the Netherlands, 44 educational institutions have been affected.<ref name="NL">{{cite web |title=Thousands of Dutch Students and Teachers Affected by ShinyHunters Hack |website=Dutch Times |date=2026-05-07 |url=https://dutchtimes.nl/news/netherlands/thousands-of-dutch-students-and-teachers-affected-by-shinyhunters-hack/ |access-date=2026-05-08}}</ref>  Several universities disconnected Canvas from their internal systems.<ref name="Telegraaf">{{cite news |last1=<!--- No author named ---> |first1=<!--- No author named ---> |title=Universiteiten koppelen systemen los na hack, gevolgen voor onderwijs |url=https://www.telegraaf.nl/binnenland/universiteiten-koppelen-systemen-los-na-hack-gevolgen-voor-onderwijs/151233814.html |access-date=8 May 2026 |publisher=Telegraaf |date=2026-05-08 |language=Dutch |trans-title=Universities disconnect systems after hack, consequences for education}}</ref>

Canvas resumed operations several hours after investigating the unauthorized access, later confirming that the exploit was caused by an issue related to its Free-For-Teacher accounts. Instructure has yet to state whether it paid a ransom nor issue an update regarding the compromised data.<ref>{{cite news|first1=Heather|last1=Hollingsworth|first2=Corey|last2=Williams|title=Canvas system is online after a cyberattack disrupted thousands of schools|publisher=AP News|url=https://apnews.com/article/canvas-cyberattack-outage-college-446c240d5aeb1b1a1e3795fb92237563|date=2026-05-08|access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a learning management system operated by its parent company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users. The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure itself reported on their status page no incidents whatsoever related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Instructure Status|date=2026-05-08|access-date=2026-05-08|url=https://status.instructure.com/|website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

The hack is the largest educational security breach on record as of May 8, 2026, given that Canvas is used by 41% of higher academia in the US alone and some [[K-12]] schools<ref name=m404>{{cite web|url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/|title=The biggest student data privacy disaster in history: Canvas hack shows the danger of centralized edtech}}</ref> with 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions being attacked worldwide. ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (some 275 million records), including private messages between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://thetechmarketer.com/canvas-hacked-instructure-shinyhunters-2026/|title=Canvas Hacked Instructure ShinyHunters 2026: 5 Alarming Facts for Students|date=May 8, 2026}}</ref>

The affair came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page. Despite the sensitivity of some of their messages, the sheer scope of the data compromised, and the [[single point of failure]], they had not been previously informed of any issues whatsoever with the platform.<ref>https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/</ref>

== Background ==
Canvas has more than 30 million global active users, and is widely used by K–12 schools, colleges, and universities in the United States for coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, grades, and communication between instructors and students.<ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref> ''[[Inside Higher Ed]]'' described Canvas as the most popular learning management system in North American higher education, reporting that it was used by about 41 percent of higher education institutions in the region.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
Instructure said the information involved in the incident appeared to include certain identifying information, such as names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages between users.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The company stated that it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/>

On May 7, Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test were placed into "scheduled" maintenance mode while Instructure investigated the issue.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Instructure Status |url=https://status.instructure.com/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

Contact information via the [[end-to-end encryption]] protocol [[Tox (protocol)|T0X]] to a [[.onion]] address is then given.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://github.com/pete-builds/research-reports/blob/main/canvas-instructure-breach-may-2026.md|title=research-reports/canvas-instructure-breach-may-2026.md at main · pete-builds/research-reports|website=GitHub}}</ref>

However, more often, a screen was shown simply saying that Canvas was down for maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 8, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>
