The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref>

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of 8 May 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref> as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

The incident came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page.<ref name="m404" />

== Background ==
In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at 8,000 educational institutions in Australia, the United States and some European nations. The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="e1">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in North American higher education where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="e1"/><ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> Canvas is used by K–12 schools and higher education.<ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref><ref name="e1" />

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1 Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 2 Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="z1"/> On May 6 the company stated their system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="s1">{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> [[Queensland Minister of Education]] [[John-Paul Langbroek]] said the attack impacted the data of 200 million people. Queensland Teachers' Union called for investigation for what caused the breach and how similar attacks could be thwarted. Both Instructure and several Australian officials commenced investigations.

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8pm eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="z1">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref>

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of 8 May 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref> as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

The incident came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page.<ref name="m404" />

== Background ==
In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="e1">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in North American higher education where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="e1"/><ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref> Canvas is used by K–12 schools and higher education.<ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |last2=Tucker |first2=Emma |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas hack strands university students during finals week |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/us/canvas-hack-strands-college-students-finals-week |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=CNN }}</ref><ref name="e1" />

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1 Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 2 Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="z1"/> On May 6 the company stated their system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="s1">{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> [[Queensland Minister of Education]] [[John-Paul Langbroek]] said the attack impacted the data of 200 million people. Queensland Teachers' Union called for investigation for what caused the breach and how similar attacks could be thwarted. Both Instructure and several Australian officials commenced investigations.

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8pm eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="z1">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

However, more often, a screen was shown simply saying that Canvas was down for maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 9, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1 Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 2 Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="z1"/> On May 6 the company stated their system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="s1">{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref> [[Queensland Minister of Education]] [[John-Paul Langbroek]] said the attack impacted the data of 200 million people. Queensland Teachers' Union called for investigation for what caused the breach and how similar attacks could be thwarted. Both Instructure and several Australian officials commenced investigations.

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref>

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of 8 May 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref> as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

The incident came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page.<ref name="m404" />

In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="e1">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in North American higher education where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="e1"/><ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

The '''2026 Canvas security incident''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref>

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of 8 May 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref> as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

The incident came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page.<ref name="m404" />

== Background ==
In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="e1">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in North American higher education where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="e1"/><ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="z1"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="s1">{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8pm eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="z1">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

However, more often, a screen was shown simply saying that Canvas was down for maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 9, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="s1">{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. The '''2026 Canvas security breach''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved in the hacking.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref>

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of 8 May 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref> as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

The incident came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page.<ref name="m404" />

== Background ==
In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="e1">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in North American higher education where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="e1"/><ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="z1"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="s1">{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8pm eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="z1">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

However, more often, a screen was shown simply saying that Canvas was down for maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 9, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

The '''2026 Canvas security breach''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved in the hacking.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref>  However, San Diego Community College District students received a message from the District, alerting them to students experiencing incidents of attempted extortion by these hackers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=mySDCCD Info Hub - mySDCCD Wiki |url=https://mysdccd.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MYS/pages/3293511703/San+Diego+Community+College+District+Cybersecurity+Update |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=mysdccd.atlassian.net}}</ref>

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of 8 May 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref> as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

The incident came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page.<ref name="m404" />

== Background ==
In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="e1">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in North American higher education where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="e1"/><ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="z1"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="s1">{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8pm eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="z1">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

However, more often, a screen was shown simply saying that Canvas was down for maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 9, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

Canvas resumed operations several hours after investigating the unauthorised access, later confirming that the exploit was caused by an issue related to its Free-For-Teacher accounts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure |language=en}}</ref> Some institutions waited to verify the security of their systems before activating Canvas on the afternoon of May 8.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oregon State University Information Services Status Dashboard |url=https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |website=Oregon State University |publisher=Oregon State University |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509043040/https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |archive-date=2026-05-09 |location=Corvallis, Oregon, United States |language=English |date=2026-05-08 |url-status=live}}</ref> Instructure has yet to state whether it paid a ransom or issue an update regarding the compromised data.<ref>{{cite news|first1=Heather|last1=Hollingsworth|first2=Corey|last2=Williams|title=Canvas system is online after a cyberattack disrupted thousands of schools|publisher=AP News|url=https://apnews.com/article/canvas-cyberattack-outage-college-446c240d5aeb1b1a1e3795fb92237563|date=2026-05-08|access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref>

== Impact ==
Educational institutions in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, New Zealand,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/education/594635/new-zealand-students-details-caught-up-in-massive-global-university-hack|title=New Zealand students' details caught up in massive global university hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=RNZ|last=Forman|first=Luka|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]]}}</ref> Australia,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234|title=Major data breach sees student details compromised|date=May 7, 2026|via=|website=ABC News|publisher=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref> Sweden,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.slu.se/en/news/2026/canvasincident/|title=Information about a cybersecurity incident related to Canvas|website=[[Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences]]}}</ref> the Netherlands,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613564-universiteiten-en-hogescholen-blokkeren-studie-app-canvas-na-hack|title=Universiteiten en hogescholen blokkeren studie-app Canvas na hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=NOS|last=Scholtens|first=Indy|language=nl|publisher=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting]]}}</ref> and Singapore<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=NUS named in global data breach list |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/nus-among-3-singapore-institutions-hit-by-global-data-breach |access-date=2026-05-09 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> reported disruptions or potential exposure of user information.

Affected academic institutions in the US include, but are not limited to, all [[Ivy League|Ivy League schools]], [[Pennsylvania State University]], [[University of Illinois]], [[James Madison University]], [[University of Nebraska-Lincoln]], [[Georgetown University]], [[Oregon State University]], [[University of Michigan]], [[Rutgers University]], [[University of California]], [[University In New Zealand, University of Auckland, AUT and the Victoria University of Wellington were affected as was Kristin School.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/education/594635/new-zealand-students-details-caught-up-in-massive-global-university-hack|title=New Zealand students' details caught up in massive global university hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=RNZ|last=Forman|first=Luka|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]]}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="z1"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="s1">{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. The '''2026 Canvas security breach''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved in the hacking.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref>  However, San Diego Community College District students received a message from the District, alerting them to students experiencing incidents of attempted extortion by these hackers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=mySDCCD Info Hub - mySDCCD Wiki |url=https://mysdccd.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MYS/pages/3293511703/San+Diego+Community+College+District+Cybersecurity+Update |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=mysdccd.atlassian.net}}</ref>

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of 8 May 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref> as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

The incident came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page.<ref name="m404" />

== Background ==
In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="e1">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in North American higher education where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="e1"/><ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="z1"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="s1">{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8pm eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="z1">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>

The '''2026 Canvas security breach''' is an ongoing cybersecurity incident, outage, and [[data breach]] affecting [[Canvas (LMS)|Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and messages among users.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved in the hacking.<ref name="auto1">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas' sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7-8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref>  However, San Diego Community College District students received a message from the District, alerting them to students experiencing incidents of attempted extortion by these hackers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=mySDCCD Info Hub - mySDCCD Wiki |url=https://mysdccd.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MYS/pages/3293511703/San+Diego+Community+College+District+Cybersecurity+Update |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=mysdccd.atlassian.net}}</ref>

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of 8 May 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref> as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

The incident came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]) when students began posting on [[Reddit]] screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page.<ref name="m404" />

== Background ==
In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="e1">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in North American higher education where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="e1"/><ref name="auto">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="z1"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="s1">{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident - Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure}}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8pm eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="z1">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name=":0"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

However, more often, a screen was shown simply saying that Canvas was down for maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 9, 2026.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="auto"/>

Canvas resumed operations several hours after investigating the unauthorised access, later confirming that the exploit was caused by an issue related to its Free-For-Teacher accounts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure |language=en}}</ref> Some institutions waited to verify the security of their systems before activating Canvas on the afternoon of May 8.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oregon State University Information Services Status Dashboard |url=https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |website=Oregon State University |publisher=Oregon State University |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509043040/https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |archive-date=2026-05-09 |location=Corvallis, Oregon, United States |language=English |date=2026-05-08 |url-status=live}}</ref> Instructure has yet to state whether it paid a ransom or issue an update regarding the compromised data.<ref>{{cite news|first1=Heather|last1=Hollingsworth|first2=Corey|last2=Williams|title=Canvas system is online after a cyberattack disrupted thousands of schools|publisher=AP News|url=https://apnews.com/article/canvas-cyberattack-outage-college-446c240d5aeb1b1a1e3795fb92237563|date=2026-05-08|access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref>
