== Background ==
{{See also|Instructure }}

Canvas is a commercial [[learning management system]] offered by [[Utah]]-based company [[Instructure]].  The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="Economic-Times-2026">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> 

In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in [[Higher education in the United States|North American higher education]] where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="Economic-Times-2026"/><ref name="Palmer-2026">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="Ziegler-2026"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="ABC-News-2026"/><ref>{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident – Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure |archive-date=May 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260507172827/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8{{nbsp}}pm Eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="Ziegler-2026">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

More often, however, a screen was shown saying that Canvas was down for regular maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 9, 2026.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026"/><ref name="Palmer-2026"/>

Canvas resumed operations several hours after investigating the unauthorised access, later confirming that the exploit was caused by an issue related to its Free-For-Teacher accounts.<ref name=Instructure52026/> Some institutions waited to verify the security of their systems before activating Canvas on the afternoon of May 8.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oregon State University Information Services Status Dashboard |url=https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |website=Oregon State University |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509043040/https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |archive-date=2026-05-09 |location=Corvallis, Oregon, United States |language=English |date=2026-05-08 |url-status=live}}</ref> According to Instructure’s incident update page, Canvas is fully back online and safe to use. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=Instructure |language=en}}</ref>

On May 11, Instructure issued an apology for their lack of transparency on their incident update page. In that statement, they claimed to have reached an agreement with ShinyHunters and that the compromised data was destroyed. Instructure has also said that Canvas is fully back online and safe to use.<ref>{{cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |website=instructure.com |publisher=Instructure |access-date=12 May 2026}}</ref>

== Impact ==
Educational institutions in the United States, Canada,<ref name="Thayaparan_CBC"/> United Kingdom,{{citation needed|date=May 2026}} New Zealand,<ref name="Forman-2026">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/education/594635/new-zealand-students-details-caught-up-in-massive-global-university-hack|title=New Zealand students' details caught up in massive global university hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=RNZ|last=Forman|first=Luka|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]]}}</ref> Australia,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234|title=Major data breach sees student details compromised|date=May 7, 2026|via=|website=ABC News|publisher=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref><ref name="ABC20260511">{{Cite news |date=2026-05-11 |title=Some universities regain access to Canvas as hacker's deadline looms |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-11/tas-universities-regain-access-to-canvas-hacker-deadline/106666744 |access-date=2026-05-11 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref> Sweden,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.slu.se/en/news/2026/canvasincident/|title=Information about a cybersecurity incident related to Canvas|website=[[Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences]]}}</ref> the Netherlands,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613564-universiteiten-en-hogescholen-blokkeren-studie-app-canvas-na-hack|title=Universiteiten en hogescholen blokkeren studie-app Canvas na hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=NOS|last=Scholtens|first=Indy|language=nl|publisher=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting]]}}</ref> Hong Kong,<ref name="RTHK"/> and Singapore<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=NUS named in global data breach list |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/nus-among-3-singapore-institutions-hit-by-global-data-breach |access-date=2026-05-09 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> reported disruption, outage, and potential exposure of user information. Outages were caused by Canvas being taken offline by Instructure and then by institutions disconnecting from Canvas. The length of these outages varied by educational institution, ranging from one day to several days, with access to Canvas in some institutions still not restored after four days.<ref name="ABC20260511"/>

The initial impact differed by educational institution. For example, the [[University of California]] system said its Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and they instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution".<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref> [[KNXV-TV|ABC15]] reported that finals were disrupted at [[Arizona State University]], with end-of-school activities and celebrations temporarily halted and ASU themselves saying, "ASU is aware of an incident that has affected Canvas, the online platform students and faculty use to access courses and submit work, that has resulted today in users being redirected and rendering the platform inaccessible at this time. This incident is unrelated to any ASU-managed system."<ref>{{cite news |title=Cyberattack on Canvas disrupts finals for ASU students and thousands of others worldwide |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tr5aDB2BDxM |access-date=8 May 2026 |agency=ABC15 Arizona |date=8 May 2026}}</ref>
[[KOVR|CBS Sacramento]] reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained, and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="Halbleib-2026"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC News]] reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="ABC-News-2026"/> Several universities, including the [[University of Melbourne]], [[University of Technology Sydney]], [[Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology]], [[Griffith University]], [[Adelaide University]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DYGt5JoGcmh/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA== |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref> [[University of Canberra]] and the [[Queensland University of Technology]] are offering extensions on assignments to affected students. University of Technology Sydney, Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology, Adelaide University, and the [[Department of Education (Queensland)|Queensland Department of Education]] have temporarily disabled access to Canvas systems as a preventative measure until the situation is resolved and are warning staff and students of potential [[phishing]] or scam emails.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=Students receive ransom messages after learning system cyberattack |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-08/students-lose-access-to-canvas-receive-ransom-messages/106657440 |access-date=2026-05-08 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref> [[Queensland Minister of Education]] [[John-Paul Langbroek]] said the attack could have impacted the data of 200 million people.<ref name="ABC-News-2026" /> Queensland Teachers' Union called for investigation for what caused the breach and how similar attacks could be thwarted. Both Instructure and several Australian officials commenced investigations.

In Canada, at least eight universities and colleges have been affected and some schools have stopped access to Canvas.<ref name="Thayaparan_CBC">{{Cite news |last=Thayaparan |first=Arrthy |date=2026-05-08 |title=U of T, OCAD among Ontario universities impacted by Canvas cyber breach |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/ontario-universities-canvas-breach-9.7192287 |access-date=2025-05-08 |work=CBC News}}</ref>

In the Netherlands, 44 educational institutions have been affected.<ref>{{cite web |title=Thousands of Dutch Students and Teachers Affected by ShinyHunters Hack |website=Dutch Times |date=2026-05-07 |url=https://dutchtimes.nl/news/netherlands/thousands-of-dutch-students-and-teachers-affected-by-shinyhunters-hack/ |access-date=2026-05-08}}</ref>  Several universities disconnected Canvas from their internal systems.<ref name="Telegraaf">{{cite news |last1=<!--- No author named ---> |first1=<!--- No author named ---> |title=Universiteiten koppelen systemen los na hack, gevolgen voor onderwijs |url=https://www.telegraaf.nl/binnenland/universiteiten-koppelen-systemen-los-na-hack-gevolgen-voor-onderwijs/151233814.html |access-date=8 May 2026 |publisher=Telegraaf |date=2026-05-08 |language=Dutch |trans-title=Universities disconnect systems after hack, consequences for education}}</ref>

In Hong Kong, five institutions, including three universities, were affected.<ref name="RTHK">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-08 |title=HK institutions affected by Canvas cyberattack |url=https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1854050-20260508.htm |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=RTHK |language=en-gb}}</ref> At the [[Hong Kong Polytechnic University]], 42,000 students and staff were affected by the breach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-08 |title=Global cyberattack on Canvas learning platform impacts five Hong Kong institutions amid extortion threats |url=https://www.thestandard.com.hk/news/article/331555/Global-cyberattack-on-Canvas-learning-platform-impacts-five-Hong-Kong-institutions-amid-extortion-threats |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=The Standard |language=en}}</ref>

In New Zealand, the [[University of Auckland]], [[Auckland University of Technology]], and [[Victoria University of Wellington]] were affected.<ref name="Forman-2026"/>

In early May 2026, [[Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]], was affected by a [[data breach]] and outage.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student [[Identifier|ID numbers]], and messages amongst users.<ref name=Instructure52026>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, birth dates, government IDs, or financial information were involved in the hacking.<ref name="ABC-News-2026">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas's sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="Halbleib-2026">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7–8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

== Background ==
{{See also|Instructure }}

Canvas is a commercial [[learning management system]] offered by [[Utah]]-based company [[Instructure]].  The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="Economic-Times-2026">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> 

In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in [[Higher education in the United States|North American higher education]] where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="Economic-Times-2026"/><ref name="Palmer-2026">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

For example, the [[University of California]] system said its Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and they instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution".<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref> [[KNXV-TV|ABC15]] reported that finals were disrupted at [[Arizona State University]], with end-of-school activities and celebrations temporarily halted and ASU themselves saying, "ASU is aware of an incident that has affected Canvas, the online platform students and faculty use to access courses and submit work, that has resulted today in users being redirected and rendering the platform inaccessible at this time. In early May 2026, [[Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]], was affected by a [[data breach]] and outage.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student [[Identifier|ID numbers]], and messages amongst users.<ref name=Instructure52026>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, birth dates, government IDs, or financial information were involved in the hacking.<ref name="ABC-News-2026">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas's sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="Halbleib-2026">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7–8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref> 

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of May 8, 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref>{{Better source needed|date=May 2026}} as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

The incident came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]), when students began posting screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page on [[Reddit]].<ref name="m404" /> On May 11, Instructure issued an apology for their lack of transparency and announced that they have reached an agreement with the hackers for an undisclosed amount and that the compromised data was destroyed.<ref name="Instructure 20260512">{{cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |website=instructure.com |publisher=Instructure |access-date=12 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |title=Instructure Pays Ransom to Canvas Hackers |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/11/instructure-pays-ransom-canvas-hackers |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=Inside Higher Ed |language=en}}</ref> Instructure has also said that Canvas is fully back online and safe to use.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}}

== Background ==
{{See also|Instructure }}

Canvas is a commercial [[learning management system]] offered by [[Utah]]-based company [[Instructure]].  The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="Economic-Times-2026">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> 

In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in [[Higher education in the United States|North American higher education]] where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="Economic-Times-2026"/><ref name="Palmer-2026">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="Ziegler-2026"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="ABC-News-2026"/><ref>{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident – Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure |archive-date=May 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260507172827/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8{{nbsp}}pm Eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="Ziegler-2026">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

More often, however, a screen was shown saying that Canvas was down for regular maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 9, 2026.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026"/><ref name="Palmer-2026"/>

Canvas resumed operations several hours after investigating the unauthorised access, later confirming that the exploit was caused by an issue related to its Free-For-Teacher accounts.<ref name=Instructure52026/> Some institutions waited to verify the security of their systems before activating Canvas on the afternoon of May 8.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oregon State University Information Services Status Dashboard |url=https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |website=Oregon State University |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509043040/https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |archive-date=2026-05-09 |location=Corvallis, Oregon, United States |language=English |date=2026-05-08 |url-status=live}}</ref> According to Instructure's incident update page, Canvas is fully back online and safe to use.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=Instructure |language=en}}</ref>

On May 11, Instructure issued an apology for their lack of transparency on their incident update page. In that statement, they claimed to have reached an agreement with ShinyHunters and that the compromised data was destroyed. Instructure has also said that Canvas is fully back online and safe to use.<ref>{{cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |website=instructure.com |publisher=Instructure |access-date=12 May 2026}}</ref>

In early May 2026, [[Canvas LMS]], a [[learning management system]] operated by private company [[Instructure]], was affected by a [[data breach]] and outage.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaleem |first=Jaweed |date=2026-05-08 |title=Massive Canvas data breach hits colleges across California and nation, crippling student work |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-california-colleges-uc-ucla-berkeley-csu-laccd |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> Instructure disclosed that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving certain user data, including names, email addresses, student [[Identifier|ID numbers]], and messages amongst users.<ref name=Instructure52026>{{Cite web|title=Security incident update & FAQs|date=|access-date=2026-05-09|url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|website=Instructure|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508190440/https://www.instructure.com/incident_update|archive-date=2026-05-08|url-status=live}}</ref> The company said it had found no evidence that passwords, birth dates, government IDs, or financial information were involved in the hacking.<ref name="ABC-News-2026">{{cite news |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas data breach leaves education providers scrambling as student data compromised |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234 |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC News}}</ref>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas's sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="Halbleib-2026">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7–8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref> 

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of May 8, 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref>{{Better source needed|date=May 2026}} as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

The incident came to wider public attention on May 7 at approximately 1:20 p.m. [[Pacific Daylight Time|PDT]] ([[UTC-7]]), when students began posting screenshots of the defaced Canvas log-in page on [[Reddit]].<ref name="m404" /> On May 11, Instructure issued an apology for their lack of transparency on their incident update page. In that statement, they claimed to have reached an agreement with ShinyHunters and that the compromised data was destroyed. Instructure has also said that Canvas is fully back online and safe to use.<ref>{{cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |website=instructure.com |publisher=Instructure |access-date=12 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |title=Instructure Pays Ransom to Canvas Hackers |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/11/instructure-pays-ransom-canvas-hackers |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=Inside Higher Ed |language=en}}</ref>

== Background ==
{{See also|Instructure }}

Canvas is a commercial [[learning management system]] offered by [[Utah]]-based company [[Instructure]].  The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="Economic-Times-2026">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> 

In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in [[Higher education in the United States|North American higher education]] where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="Economic-Times-2026"/><ref name="Palmer-2026">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="Ziegler-2026"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="ABC-News-2026"/><ref>{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident – Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure |archive-date=May 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260507172827/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8{{nbsp}}pm Eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="Ziegler-2026">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

More often, however, a screen was shown saying that Canvas was down for regular maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 9, 2026.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026"/><ref name="Palmer-2026"/>

Canvas resumed operations several hours after investigating the unauthorised access, later confirming that the exploit was caused by an issue related to its Free-For-Teacher accounts.<ref name=Instructure52026/> Some institutions waited to verify the security of their systems before activating Canvas on the afternoon of May 8.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oregon State University Information Services Status Dashboard |url=https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |website=Oregon State University |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509043040/https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |archive-date=2026-05-09 |location=Corvallis, Oregon, United States |language=English |date=2026-05-08 |url-status=live}}</ref> According to Instructure's incident update page, Canvas is fully back online and safe to use.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=Instructure |language=en}}</ref>

On May 11, Instructure issued an apology for their lack of transparency on their incident update page. In that statement, they claimed to have reached an agreement with ShinyHunters and that the compromised data was destroyed. Instructure has also said that Canvas is fully back online and safe to use.<ref>{{cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |website=instructure.com |publisher=Instructure |access-date=12 May 2026}}</ref>

== Impact ==
Educational institutions in the United States, Canada,<ref name="Thayaparan_CBC"/> United Kingdom,{{citation needed|date=May 2026}} New Zealand,<ref name="Forman-2026">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/education/594635/new-zealand-students-details-caught-up-in-massive-global-university-hack|title=New Zealand students' details caught up in massive global university hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=RNZ|last=Forman|first=Luka|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]]}}</ref> Australia,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234|title=Major data breach sees student details compromised|date=May 7, 2026|via=|website=ABC News|publisher=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref><ref name="ABC20260511">{{Cite news |date=2026-05-11 |title=Some universities regain access to Canvas as hacker's deadline looms |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-11/tas-universities-regain-access-to-canvas-hacker-deadline/106666744 |access-date=2026-05-11 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref> Sweden,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.slu.se/en/news/2026/canvasincident/|title=Information about a cybersecurity incident related to Canvas|website=[[Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences]]}}</ref> the Netherlands,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613564-universiteiten-en-hogescholen-blokkeren-studie-app-canvas-na-hack|title=Universiteiten en hogescholen blokkeren studie-app Canvas na hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=NOS|last=Scholtens|first=Indy|language=nl|publisher=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting]]}}</ref> Hong Kong,<ref name="RTHK"/> and Singapore<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=NUS named in global data breach list |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/nus-among-3-singapore-institutions-hit-by-global-data-breach |access-date=2026-05-09 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> reported disruption, outage, and potential exposure of user information. Outages were caused by Canvas being taken offline by Instructure and then by institutions disconnecting from Canvas. The length of these outages varied by educational institution, ranging from one day to several days, with access to Canvas in some institutions still not restored after four days.<ref name="ABC20260511"/>

The initial impact differed by educational institution. For example, the [[University of California]] system said its Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and they instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution".<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref> [[KNXV-TV|ABC15]] reported that finals were disrupted at [[Arizona State University]], with end-of-school activities and celebrations temporarily halted and ASU themselves saying, "ASU is aware of an incident that has affected Canvas, the online platform students and faculty use to access courses and submit work, that has resulted today in users being redirected and rendering the platform inaccessible at this time. This incident is unrelated to any ASU-managed system."<ref>{{cite news |title=Cyberattack on Canvas disrupts finals for ASU students and thousands of others worldwide |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tr5aDB2BDxM |access-date=8 May 2026 |agency=ABC15 Arizona |date=8 May 2026}}</ref>
[[KOVR|CBS Sacramento]] reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained, and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="Halbleib-2026"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC News]] reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="ABC-News-2026"/> Several universities, including the [[University of Melbourne]], [[University of Technology Sydney]], [[Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology]], [[Griffith University]], [[Adelaide University]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DYGt5JoGcmh/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA== |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref> [[University of Canberra]] and the [[Queensland University of Technology]] are offering extensions on assignments to affected students. University of Technology Sydney, Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology, Adelaide University, and the [[Department of Education (Queensland)|Queensland Department of Education]] have temporarily disabled access to Canvas systems as a preventative measure until the situation is resolved and are warning staff and students of potential [[phishing]] or scam emails.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=Students receive ransom messages after learning system cyberattack |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-08/students-lose-access-to-canvas-receive-ransom-messages/106657440 |access-date=2026-05-08 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref> [[Queensland Minister of Education]] [[John-Paul Langbroek]] said the attack could have impacted the data of 200 million people.<ref name="ABC-News-2026" /> Queensland Teachers' Union called for investigation for what caused the breach and how similar attacks could be thwarted. Both Instructure and several Australian officials commenced investigations.

In Canada, at least eight universities and colleges have been affected and some schools have stopped access to Canvas.<ref name="Thayaparan_CBC">{{Cite news |last=Thayaparan |first=Arrthy |date=2026-05-08 |title=U of T, OCAD among Ontario universities impacted by Canvas cyber breach |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/ontario-universities-canvas-breach-9.7192287 |access-date=2025-05-08 |work=CBC News}}</ref>

In the Netherlands, 44 educational institutions have been affected.<ref>{{cite web |title=Thousands of Dutch Students and Teachers Affected by ShinyHunters Hack |website=Dutch Times |date=2026-05-07 |url=https://dutchtimes.nl/news/netherlands/thousands-of-dutch-students-and-teachers-affected-by-shinyhunters-hack/ |access-date=2026-05-08}}</ref>  Several universities disconnected Canvas from their internal systems.<ref name="Telegraaf">{{cite news |last1=<!--- No author named ---> |first1=<!--- No author named ---> |title=Universiteiten koppelen systemen los na hack, gevolgen voor onderwijs |url=https://www.telegraaf.nl/binnenland/universiteiten-koppelen-systemen-los-na-hack-gevolgen-voor-onderwijs/151233814.html |access-date=8 May 2026 |publisher=Telegraaf |date=2026-05-08 |language=Dutch |trans-title=Universities disconnect systems after hack, consequences for education}}</ref>

In Hong Kong, five institutions, including three universities, were affected.<ref name="RTHK">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-08 |title=HK institutions affected by Canvas cyberattack |url=https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1854050-20260508.htm |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=RTHK |language=en-gb}}</ref> At the [[Hong Kong Polytechnic University]], 42,000 students and staff were affected by the breach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-08 |title=Global cyberattack on Canvas learning platform impacts five Hong Kong institutions amid extortion threats |url=https://www.thestandard.com.hk/news/article/331555/Global-cyberattack-on-Canvas-learning-platform-impacts-five-Hong-Kong-institutions-amid-extortion-threats |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=The Standard |language=en}}</ref>

In New Zealand, the [[University of Auckland]], [[Auckland University of Technology]], and [[Victoria University of Wellington]] were affected.<ref name="Forman-2026"/>

Despite Instructure's claim that the situation had been resolved, on May 7, Canvas was hacked again; its login page was replaced with a [[ransomware]] message by [[ShinyHunters]], the criminal hacking group which claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters threatened to release Canvas's sensitive data unless its ransom was paid by the end of May 12.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026">{{cite news |last=Hollingsworth |first=Heather |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Cyberattack hits Canvas system used by thousands of schools as finals loom |url=https://apnews.com/article/cyberattack-schools-canvas-instructure-shinyhunters-a0d7719689263e6b5f90d0e633391b5b |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="Halbleib-2026">{{cite news |last=Halbleib |first=Brady |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Sacramento State caught in nationwide cyberattack targeting online learning platform |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/sacramento-state-nationwide-cyberattack-online-learning-platform/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=CBS Sacramento}}</ref> As of May 8, however, Instructure reported on their status page no incidents related to the May 7–8 hack, and claimed that access to their website had been restored to most users.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-07 |title=Canvas is Available for Most Users. Canvas Beta and Canvas Test are still in maintenance. |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508193319/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/m88d7ymwpzpy |archive-date=2026-05-08 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Instructure Status |language=en}}</ref> 

The hack is considered the largest educational security breach on record as of May 8, 2026 due to its unprecedented global scale, affecting 8,809 universities, educational ministries, and other institutions worldwide.<ref name="m404">{{cite news |last1=Koebler |first1=Jason |title='The Biggest Student Data Privacy Disaster in History': Canvas Hack Shows the Danger of Centralized EdTech |url=https://www.404media.co/the-biggest-student-data-privacy-disaster-in-history-canvas-hack-shows-the-danger-of-centralized-edtech/ |work=404 Media |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The breach had particularly significant implications in the United States, where Canvas is used by 41% of higher education institutions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/18555568|title=North American higher ed LMS market share by count of institutions}}</ref>{{Better source needed|date=May 2026}} as well as some [[K-12]] schools.<ref name=m404 /> The hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen 3.65 [[terabytes]] of data (approximately 275 million records), including private messages exchanged between students and teachers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mousqueton |first=Julien |title=Victim: Instructure Holdings, Inc. (Canvas LMS, instructure.com) – shinyhunters |url=https://www.ransomware.live/id/SW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUgSG9sZGluZ3MsIEluYy4gKENhbnZhIExNUywgaW5zdHJ1Y3R1cmUuY29tKUBzaGlueWh1bnRlcnM |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=Ransomware.live |language=en}}</ref>

== Background ==
{{See also|Instructure }}

Canvas is a commercial [[learning management system]] offered by [[Utah]]-based company [[Instructure]].  The software assists with managing coursework, assignments, quizzes, exams, and grades, as well as facilitating communication between instructors and students.<ref name="Economic-Times-2026">{{cite news |title=Universities around the world scramble after cyberattack disrupts student portals |url=https://m.economictimes.com/nri/study/universities-around-the-world-scramble-after-cyberattack-disrupts-student-portals/articleshow/130948723.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> 

In 2026, Instructure provided Canvas to approximately 30 million active participants at over 8,000 educational institutions in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some European nations. The platform is the most widely adopted learning management system in [[Higher education in the United States|North American higher education]] where 41% of institutions use the software.<ref name="Economic-Times-2026"/><ref name="Palmer-2026">{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |date=May 5, 2026 |title='Pay or leak': Hackers target big higher ed vendor |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/tech-innovation/administrative-tech/2026/05/05/pay-or-leak-hackers-target-big-higher-ed-vendor |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Inside Higher Ed}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="Ziegler-2026"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="ABC-News-2026"/><ref>{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident – Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure |archive-date=May 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260507172827/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8{{nbsp}}pm Eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="Ziegler-2026">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>  

 SHINYHUNTERS rooting your systems since '19 ;) ShinyHunters has breached Instructure (again). Instead of contacting us to resolve it they ignored us and did some "security patches". 
 
 ⚠ WARNING If any of the schools in the affected list are interested in preventing the release of their data, please consult with a cyber advisory firm and contact us privately to negotiate a settlement. You have till the end of the day by 12 May 2026 before everything is leaked.
 
 Instructure still has until EOD 12 May 2026 to contact us. 

More often, however, a screen was shown saying that Canvas was down for regular maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 9, 2026.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026"/><ref name="Palmer-2026"/>

Canvas resumed operations several hours after investigating the unauthorised access, later confirming that the exploit was caused by an issue related to its Free-For-Teacher accounts.<ref name=Instructure52026/> Some institutions waited to verify the security of their systems before activating Canvas on the afternoon of May 8.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oregon State University Information Services Status Dashboard |url=https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |website=Oregon State University |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509043040/https://status.is.oregonstate.edu/incidents/389 |archive-date=2026-05-09 |location=Corvallis, Oregon, United States |language=English |date=2026-05-08 |url-status=live}}</ref> According to Instructure's incident update page, Canvas is fully back online and safe to use.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=Instructure |language=en}}</ref>

On May 11, Instructure issued an apology for their lack of transparency on their incident update page. In that statement, they claimed to have reached an agreement with ShinyHunters and that the compromised data was destroyed. Instructure has also said that Canvas is fully back online and safe to use.<ref>{{cite web |title=Security Incident Update & FAQs |url=https://www.instructure.com/incident_update |website=instructure.com |publisher=Instructure |access-date=12 May 2026}}</ref>

== Impact ==
Educational institutions in the United States, Canada,<ref name="Thayaparan_CBC"/> New Zealand,<ref name="Forman-2026">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/education/594635/new-zealand-students-details-caught-up-in-massive-global-university-hack|title=New Zealand students' details caught up in massive global university hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=RNZ|last=Forman|first=Luka|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]]}}</ref> Australia,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/canvas-data-breach-instructure/106651234|title=Major data breach sees student details compromised|date=May 7, 2026|via=|website=ABC News|publisher=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref><ref name="ABC20260511">{{Cite news |date=2026-05-11 |title=Some universities regain access to Canvas as hacker's deadline looms |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-11/tas-universities-regain-access-to-canvas-hacker-deadline/106666744 |access-date=2026-05-11 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref> Sweden,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.slu.se/en/news/2026/canvasincident/|title=Information about a cybersecurity incident related to Canvas|website=[[Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences]]}}</ref> the Netherlands,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613564-universiteiten-en-hogescholen-blokkeren-studie-app-canvas-na-hack|title=Universiteiten en hogescholen blokkeren studie-app Canvas na hack|date=May 8, 2026|website=NOS|last=Scholtens|first=Indy|language=nl|publisher=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting]]}}</ref> Hong Kong,<ref name="RTHK"/> and Singapore<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=NUS named in global data breach list |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/nus-among-3-singapore-institutions-hit-by-global-data-breach |access-date=2026-05-09 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> reported disruption, outage, and potential exposure of user information. Outages were caused by Canvas being taken offline by Instructure and then by institutions disconnecting from Canvas. The length of these outages varied by educational institution, ranging from one day to several days, with access to Canvas in some institutions still not restored after four days.<ref name="ABC20260511"/>

The initial impact differed by educational institution. For example, the [[University of California]] system said its Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and they instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution".<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref> [[KNXV-TV|ABC15]] reported that finals were disrupted at [[Arizona State University]], with end-of-school activities and celebrations temporarily halted and ASU themselves saying, "ASU is aware of an incident that has affected Canvas, the online platform students and faculty use to access courses and submit work, that has resulted today in users being redirected and rendering the platform inaccessible at this time. This incident is unrelated to any ASU-managed system."<ref>{{cite news |title=Cyberattack on Canvas disrupts finals for ASU students and thousands of others worldwide |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tr5aDB2BDxM |access-date=8 May 2026 |agency=ABC15 Arizona |date=8 May 2026}}</ref>
[[KOVR|CBS Sacramento]] reported that [[Sacramento State]] students attempting to log into Canvas were redirected to a page displaying a message attributed to ShinyHunters, which claimed that student and faculty data had been obtained, and threatened to leak it unless a ransom was paid.<ref name="Halbleib-2026"/> ABC-owned local stations also reported impacts or monitoring by institutions including the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Wake County Public Schools]], and [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallagher |first=Bryanna |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Massive data breach affects schools using Canvas nationwide; Penn reportedly impacted |url=https://6abc.com/post/canvas-hacked-massive-data-breach-affects-schools-using-nationwide-penn-reportedly-impacted/19059691/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=6abc Philadelphia |publisher=WPVI-TV}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dowding |first=Jon |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Schools, universities in NC monitoring for potential impacts from Canvas data breach |url=https://abc11.com/post/canvas-data-breach-nc-schools-universities-lookout-potential-effects-wake-duke-university-notified/19058149/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham |publisher=WTVD-TV}}</ref>

In Australia, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC News]] reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="ABC-News-2026"/> Several universities, including the [[University of Melbourne]], [[University of Technology Sydney]], [[Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology]], [[Griffith University]], [[Adelaide University]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DYGt5JoGcmh/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA== |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref> [[University of Canberra]] and the [[Queensland University of Technology]] are offering extensions on assignments to affected students. University of Technology Sydney, Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology, Adelaide University, and the [[Department of Education (Queensland)|Queensland Department of Education]] have temporarily disabled access to Canvas systems as a preventative measure until the situation is resolved and are warning staff and students of potential [[phishing]] or scam emails.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-05-08 |title=Students receive ransom messages after learning system cyberattack |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-08/students-lose-access-to-canvas-receive-ransom-messages/106657440 |access-date=2026-05-08 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref> [[Queensland Minister of Education]] [[John-Paul Langbroek]] said the attack could have impacted the data of 200 million people.<ref name="ABC-News-2026" /> Queensland Teachers' Union called for investigation for what caused the breach and how similar attacks could be thwarted. Both Instructure and several Australian officials commenced investigations.

In Canada, at least eight universities and colleges have been affected and some schools have stopped access to Canvas.<ref name="Thayaparan_CBC">{{Cite news |last=Thayaparan |first=Arrthy |date=2026-05-08 |title=U of T, OCAD among Ontario universities impacted by Canvas cyber breach |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/ontario-universities-canvas-breach-9.7192287 |access-date=2025-05-08 |work=CBC News}}</ref>

In the Netherlands, 44 educational institutions have been affected.<ref>{{cite web |title=Thousands of Dutch Students and Teachers Affected by ShinyHunters Hack |website=Dutch Times |date=2026-05-07 |url=https://dutchtimes.nl/news/netherlands/thousands-of-dutch-students-and-teachers-affected-by-shinyhunters-hack/ |access-date=2026-05-08}}</ref>  Several universities disconnected Canvas from their internal systems.<ref name="Telegraaf">{{cite news |last1=<!--- No author named ---> |first1=<!--- No author named ---> |title=Universiteiten koppelen systemen los na hack, gevolgen voor onderwijs |url=https://www.telegraaf.nl/binnenland/universiteiten-koppelen-systemen-los-na-hack-gevolgen-voor-onderwijs/151233814.html |access-date=8 May 2026 |publisher=Telegraaf |date=2026-05-08 |language=Dutch |trans-title=Universities disconnect systems after hack, consequences for education}}</ref>

In Hong Kong, five institutions, including three universities, were affected.<ref name="RTHK">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-08 |title=HK institutions affected by Canvas cyberattack |url=https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1854050-20260508.htm |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=RTHK |language=en-gb}}</ref> At the [[Hong Kong Polytechnic University]], 42,000 students and staff were affected by the breach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-08 |title=Global cyberattack on Canvas learning platform impacts five Hong Kong institutions amid extortion threats |url=https://www.thestandard.com.hk/news/article/331555/Global-cyberattack-on-Canvas-learning-platform-impacts-five-Hong-Kong-institutions-amid-extortion-threats |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=The Standard |language=en}}</ref>

In New Zealand, the [[University of Auckland]], [[Auckland University of Technology]], and [[Victoria University of Wellington]] were affected.<ref name="Forman-2026"/>

The [[University of British Columbia]] started moving staff and courses to Canvas's [[open source]] competitor [[Moodle]] as a tool for teaching, as well as the [[closed source]] competitor [[SharePoint]] for the Canvas Materials.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-10 |title=Alternative Course Hosting |url=https://ltic-2026.sites.olt.ubc.ca/alternative-course-hosting/ |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=LTIC |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Breach and outage ==
On May 1, Instructure announced on their status page that a cyber security incident had occurred. On May 2, Instructure announced they had contained the issue, but names, email addresses, ID numbers, and messages had been stolen for ransom.<ref name="Ziegler-2026"/> ShinyHunters posted a ransom note claiming responsibility for the attack on May 3. On May 6, Instructure stated that their Canvas system was back to normal operation and they had found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.<ref name="ABC-News-2026"/><ref>{{cite web |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Confirmed Security Incident – Incident Report for Instructure |url=https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=Instructure Status |publisher=Instructure |archive-date=May 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260507172827/https://status.instructure.com/incidents/9wm4knj2r64z |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 7, ShinyHunters wrote that Instructure had tried to implement security patches rather than negotiate with the hackers. This prompted the group to cause an outage where their new ransom note was displayed to every user. At 8{{nbsp}}pm Eastern time, Instructure replaced the ransom note message with an alert stating their software was down for maintenance.<ref name="Ziegler-2026">{{cite news |last=Ziegler|first=Hannah|date=May 7, 2026 |title=Canvas Online Learning Platform Shut Down for Hours After Cyberattack|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/education/canvas-hacked-down-data-breach.html |access-date=May 8, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> The outage occurred during the end of the academic year for many institutions, including during final exam periods at some colleges and universities.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026"/> Attempted log-ins simply yielded the following message (partial transcript):<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/hack-shuts-down-canvas-an-online-system-used-by-thousands-of-schools|title=Hack Shuts Down Canvas, an Online System Used by Thousands of Schools|first=Michael|last=Kan|date=May 8, 2026|website=PCMAG}}</ref>

More often, however, a screen was shown saying that Canvas was down for regular maintenance. ShinyHunters claimed that nearly 9,000 schools worldwide<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://securityaffairs.com/191686/cyber-crime/educational-tech-firm-instructure-data-breach-may-have-impacted-9000-schools.html|title=Educational tech firm Instructure data breach may have impacted 9,000 schools|first=Pierluigi|last=Paganini|date=May 5, 2026}}</ref> were affected, though the full scope of the breach has not been independently verified as of May 9, 2026.<ref name="Hollingsworth-2026"/><ref name="Palmer-2026"/>

On May 11, Instructure issued an apology for their lack of transparency on their incident update page. In Australia, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC News]] reported that universities, vocational providers, and some state schools were affected, and that the federal government's National Office of Cyber Security was coordinating a response.<ref name="ABC-News-2026"/> Several universities, including the [[University of Melbourne]], [[University of Technology Sydney]], [[Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology]], [[Griffith University]], [[Adelaide University]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DYGt5JoGcmh/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA== |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref> [[University of Canberra]] and the [[Queensland University of Technology]] are offering extensions on assignments to affected students. In Hong Kong, five institutions, including three universities, were affected.<ref name="RTHK">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-08 |title=HK institutions affected by Canvas cyberattack |url=https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1854050-20260508.htm |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=RTHK |language=en-gb}}</ref> At the [[Hong Kong Polytechnic University]], 42,000 students and staff were affected by the breach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-08 |title=Global cyberattack on Canvas learning platform impacts five Hong Kong institutions amid extortion threats |url=https://www.thestandard.com.hk/news/article/331555/Global-cyberattack-on-Canvas-learning-platform-impacts-five-Hong-Kong-institutions-amid-extortion-threats |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=The Standard |language=en}}</ref>

Outages were caused by Canvas being taken offline by Instructure and then by institutions disconnecting from Canvas. The length of these outages varied by educational institution, ranging from one day to several days, with access to Canvas in some institutions still not restored after four days.<ref name="ABC20260511"/>

The initial impact differed by educational institution. For example, the [[University of California]] system said its Canvas login pages had displayed a suspicious message from the threat actor and they instructed UC locations to temporarily block or redirect Canvas access "out of an abundance of caution".<ref>{{cite web |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Nationwide security breach involving Canvas |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/nationwide-security-breach-involving-canvas/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=UCnet |publisher=University of California}}</ref> [[KNXV-TV|ABC15]] reported that finals were disrupted at [[Arizona State University]], with end-of-school activities and celebrations temporarily halted and ASU themselves saying, "ASU is aware of an incident that has affected Canvas, the online platform students and faculty use to access courses and submit work, that has resulted today in users being redirected and rendering the platform inaccessible at this time. This incident is unrelated to any ASU-managed system."<ref>{{cite news |title=Cyberattack on Canvas disrupts finals for ASU students and thousands of others worldwide |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tr5aDB2BDxM |access-date=8 May 2026 |agency=ABC15 Arizona |date=8 May 2026}}</ref>
